newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Call liquidation crushes US T-bond vols.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call liquidation crushes US T-bond vols.

text.p: A rush to liquidate call positions that had been accumulated ahead of today's October U.S. employment report crushed implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options, dealers said.
A downturn in bond prices after an early rally on the jobs data accelerated the selling in options that had already been under pressure from weekend time-decay, they added.
"There was a chunk of people getting out of long positions," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options fell a quarter point to 9.95 percent and December, which only have two weeks to maturity, plunged by over a full point to 9.75.
Shorter-dated options have higher gamma implications than longer maturities, providing larger movement in premiums on a swing in bond prices, but are more vulnerable to time decay.

December T-bond futures, which started the week at around 111, spiked up to just below 114 on the non-farm payrolls number early in the session. But the market soon lost steam and was later hammered by an above-50 reading in the National Association of Purchasing Management index.

Payrolls rose 210,000 in October against a forecast gain of 212,000 and September's revised decline of 35,000. October NAPM index came in at 50.2, above the 50-level, which suggests an expansion in the manufacturing economy.
Traders said volatilities were still underpinned by concerns over next week's Treasury refunding and U.S. elections.

While a widely expected re-election of President Clinton would be largely market-neutral, many traders said it could stir some inflation concerns if it was combined with a return of the Democrats to congressional majority.
In the Eurodollar pit at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, implied volatilities were also hit by call selling and the time-decay factor.
"I don't know if it was profit-taking, but the risk premium for the event was taken out of the market," an investment bank trader at CME said.
Implied volatility for March Eurodollar futures options was down 0.4 point to 13.7 percent in late trade.
But the CME trader said March volatility recovered from mid-morning lows after a 2,500-lot purchase of March 94.50 straddles by another investment bank.
"There was some buying interest after volatilities came down," he said.
